assets.alt: One cookie or bearer credential passes through transport validation, CSRF protection where required, and the route's declared assurance checks to establish an immutable principal. The principal contains identity and assurance, not permission. The owning use case combines it with an action and exact resource, reads current PostgreSQL authority, and durably records allow or deny.
assets.caption: Transport proof establishes an immutable principal, not permission. The owning use case separately evaluates current action-and-resource authority and can proceed only after its allow decision is durably recorded.

privacy_review.basis: Contains canonical domain labels and generic relationship descriptions only; no Institution, Academic Unit, Programme, Class, User, enrollment, or operational data.

assets.alt: One Institution owns a hierarchy of Academic Units. Each Academic Unit may own child units and Programmes; each Programme owns Programme Levels; and each Class is one concrete roster under a Programme Level. Academic Periods may be Institution-owned and apply everywhere, or Academic-Unit-owned and apply to that unit and its descendants. Every Class explicitly names exactly one Academic Period applicable to its Programme's Academic Unit.
assets.caption: Academic Units may recurse, but Programme, Programme Level, and Class ownership is singular. A Class explicitly names one applicable Institution- or Academic-Unit-owned Period; Proctor never infers a global current Period.

assets.alt: An Exam owns one mutable revision-fenced Draft. Publishing freezes an immutable numbered Exam Revision before an Exam Sitting selects it with one eligible Class and an explicit time window. assets.caption: Publishing separates mutable authoring from immutable delivery. Sitting and Attempt transitions remain PostgreSQL-authoritative, and both voluntary submission and automatic Sitting closure converge on one terminal Submission with no reopen or resubmission.

assets.alt: A client request passes through the HTTP transport boundary and the owning application use case before PostgreSQL commits authoritative state, audit, and durable Job or mail intent. Cache, cluster, WebSocket, and SMTP effects follow the commit and are reconstructible or best effort. Problem Details and a request ID identify transport failures, durable records prove the committed outcome, and metrics or bounded logs explain effect delivery.

assets.alt: A Session-authenticated User Settings replacement passes from strict HTTP decoding to the owning self-service application use case, which refers to the domain model and prepares audit and idempotency before calling a named Store replacement. PostgreSQL locks the current document and commits the source, audit, and replay outcome before a best-effort realtime refetch hint is published.
assets.caption: Each boundary owns one part of the replacement. PostgreSQL makes the source, audit, and replay outcome authoritative; realtime publishes only a post-commit refetch hint and never the settings source.

assets.alt: A password-reset credential arrives in a masked URL fragment. The root removes the complete fragment before parsing one purpose-specific token. assets.caption: Credential sanitation happens before rendering. The feature then maps one bounded HTTP result into the exact terminal or recoverable state that owns the next focus and secret-lifetime decision.
